rules.statement: When issuing a shared secret that an external party presents verbatim (such as an OAuth client_secret), generate a URL-safe random string, reveal that string, and store exactly its UTF-8 bytes as the key material, never raw random bytes revealed as base64url.
rules.why: client_secret_basic/post compare UTF8(presented secret) to the stored bytes, and client_secret_jwt (OIDC Core §9) uses the UTF-8 octets of the client_secret as the HS256 key. Because UTF8(base64url(raw)) ≠ raw, a secret stored as raw bytes can never authenticate.
rules.check: Look for client-secret issuance paths (dynamic client registration, management create-secret endpoints, seeding) that generate raw CSPRNG bytes, store them, and return base64url(bytes) as the client_secret, or that use the cryptographic-key generation path for a client's symmetric secret.

rules.statement: Keep shared-secret generation separate from symmetric cryptographic-key generation: server-side keys (HS256 signing keys, symmetric JWE keys) store raw CSPRNG bytes and reveal their base64url (JWK `k`) form, and each call site picks the operation that matches the secret's purpose.
rules.why: Running both purposes through one generation path caused the raw-bytes defect. Making the distinction explicit at the call site stops future issuers from bringing it back.
rules.check: Look for a single generic generator used for both client secrets and server/tenant/resource-server keys, or for a server-side symmetric key that is stored as UTF-8 of a string instead of raw random bytes.

rules.statement: Persist a given (imported or seeded) shared-secret string through the same internal construction used to generate shared secrets, rather than re-implementing the encoding, data-protection and wrapping logic inline.
rules.why: Sharing one construction means the stored UTF-8 shape cannot drift between generated and imported secrets.
rules.check: Look for seed handlers, test factories or import code that build persisted secret records by hand (encoding to UTF-8, data-protecting and wrapping inline) instead of calling the shared import operation.
